biggest_catch: BetaFamily never publishes a fixed per-test payout — each developer sets the reward on each test individually, so there is no company-guaranteed amount to verify against. The catalog's '$5-$20+ per test' is a third-party estimate, not an official term.
catches: No official per-test payout schedule exists — rewards vary per test, set by each developer; you only learn the amount when browsing a specific test listing.
BetaFamily charges developers a 10% service fee on top of the tester budget — platform economics confirmed, tester payout terms are not.
Test availability is irregular; you must apply per test and can be rejected.
Work is variable by design: nothing is guaranteed and pay depends entirely on which tests you get accepted to.

c1.evidence: BetaFamily — privately held company The β Family AB (Stockholm, Sweden); operating crowdtesting platform at betafamily.com with official FAQ and active test listings.

c2.evidence: FAILED — the official FAQ publishes no fixed tester payout. Developer-side FAQ states: 'You decide how much you are willing to pay each tester.' Rewards are per-test, developer-set, and shown only on individual test listings; no concrete payout figure is published by the company.

c3.evidence: Free for testers to join; no participation fee.

c4.evidence: Official FAQ obtained (mybendahara.betafamily.com/faq): confirms testers 'can earn money testing new apps' and developers set the reward; confirms the platform but not a concrete payout.

eligibility: iOS or Android device; sign up as a beta tester; apply per test; developers select testers.
notes: Real, operating company — but rejected under the strict rule (concrete payout terms published by the company itself). Third-party reviews cite ~$10/30-min test paid via PayPal, but those figures are not company-published. Consistent with the Nielsen precedent: legit company, no concrete payout in official terms.

s1.note: Apply per test; developers select testers; availability varies by test and platform.

s2.note: No upfront fee; no company-published fee schedule for testers (the 10% service fee is charged to developers, not testers).

s3.note: Timing stated per individual test listing only — no official general payout-timing term.

s4.note: Official copy says testers 'earn money testing new apps' / 'earn rewards by writing a test report' — vague reward wording, no amounts.

s5.note: https://betafamily.com — official site, loaded live; official FAQ at mybendahara.betafamily.com/faq.

s6.note: General steps exist (sign up, apply, test, report) but no concrete payout step can be written from official terms.

s7.note: Official site and FAQ crawled live within 2 days of the check (2026-09-23).

timing: No official general payout-timing term; stated per individual test listing only.
